imagePrompt: Create one 1536 x 1024 pixel painted scene sheet, EXACTLY TWO COLUMNS BY THREE ROWS, six equal-width WIDE cinematic panels in row-major order 0 to 5. Each column is 768 pixels; rows are approximately 341, 341 and 342 pixels high. Hard straight cell edges; no gutters, no panel labels, no numbers, no captions, no typography, no readable lettering, no logos. Every cell is its own complete environment, never a sprite or a cutout. Use the polished watercolor and fine ink on textured cream paper style of Enough: warm directional light, deep teal and umber shadows, restrained paper grain, expressive natural faces, subtle imperfect painted edges. Human anatomy is believable, heads naturally sized; shoulders, elbows, wrists, hands, hips and knees belong to one continuous body. Seat hips on the actual seat, feet on the same floor, fingers visibly holding their actual objects; no disembodied hands, duplicated limbs, floating props or pasted-on heads. Keep important faces, hands, contact points and grounded figures within each wide panel with safe margins. Maintain the same identities, clothing, figure scale, prop design and spatial continuity across all six scenes. Anonymous original visual casting only, not likenesses of credited storytellers. This is a dramatic storyboard adaptation, not a claim that imagined symbols or staged details are verified events. Story: Butterfly. Palette accents: #D9E7CB, #3C6F79, #E5A1AD. Identity continuity: STUDENT: The same adult male acting student with tan skin, short dark hair, muted lavender casual top, slate trousers and plain sneakers. He remains the same ordinary person as his movement grows less guarded; no literal wings or butterfly costume. TEACHER: The same adult woman with deeper warm brown skin, long dark hair, coral top and slate skirt, practical shoes; sincere, encouraging, physically grounded and willing to look awkward herself. TOP LEFT (frame 0): On an open grassy soccer field under soft daylight, the acting student stands rigid with arms close to his sides and toes planted too carefully. A fraternity house sits far beyond the field edge, no identifiable people in its windows. The teacher waits a few paces away, ordinary-sized and relaxed. His wary eyes go toward the distant building while open grass gives his inhibited body too much exposure. Preserve believable perspective and actual distance across the field. TOP RIGHT (frame 1): The teacher demonstrates a small butterfly-like arm movement with naturally bent elbows, one wrist softly raised and the other lower, knees loose and feet grounded in grass. Her expression is earnest, not polished or mocking. The student watches from the same few paces away, shoulders still tight. The distant house remains visible but does not become a looming fantasy monster. Arms remain complete human arms; the gesture supplies all the wings needed. MIDDLE LEFT (frame 2): The student turns his head from the distant house back to the teacher, one hand half-raised in an embarrassed question while the other hangs tensely. The teacher has stopped demonstrating and stands patiently with open hands low beside her body, leaving him room to decide. Both full bodies share the same field ground plane. His raised brows and self-conscious mouth carry the fear of being watched; no actual laughing onlookers are introduced. MIDDLE RIGHT (frame 3): The student attempts a tiny uneven flap, elbows held awkwardly away from his ribs and hands bent as he takes a cautious short step. His torso is still stiff, sneakers contact the grass naturally and the arms remain visibly joined at both shoulders. The teacher watches without laughing, a few paces behind. The smallness of the motion and his concentrated face make embarrassment legible without turning his body into a caricature. BOTTOM LEFT (frame 4): The student now opens his shoulders and makes a broad, asymmetrical sweep of both human arms while stepping into the open field, one heel lifting and the other foot bearing weight. His face shows effort and a surprised emerging smile. The teacher remains behind near their starting point, watching supportively. Grass bends under actual shoes; no floating body, costume wings or magic butterflies. The distant house is smaller in the composition because his action has taken attention. BOTTOM RIGHT (frame 5): The student has crossed a real modest stretch of the soccer field, seen in a wider lateral view with the teacher much farther behind. He continues an imperfect sweeping arm motion, knees loose, one sneaker planted and one stepping, with the relaxed focused smile of someone absorbed. His lavender shirt and identity are unchanged. The fraternity house is merely background architecture. End in the moving human body, not a perfect dancer or an applauding audience. Story-specific safeguards: No literal wings, magical transformation, mocking audience or new public triumph. This is an acting exercise on a field, not a dance show. The distant fraternity house is a source of self-conscious attention, not evidence that anyone actually watched or jeered.
